title: Capacity-preserving upgrade allocator for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Asha Nair
description:
Problem: Past upgrades to dedicated GPU pools have induced short-lived capacity cliffs during node drains, causing tail latency spikes for latency-sensitive tenants and triggering customer incidents. We need a rollout mechanism that guarantees per-pool preserved capacity and coordinates with the cluster autoscaler so total available qps remains within allowed SLA windows during upgrades.

Goal: Implement an 'upgrade allocator' that can schedule pool upgrades with soft-preserved capacity, per-tenant admission reservations, and an autoscaler handshake so drains never cause sustained capacity loss. The allocator should be LTS-aware (allowing different rollout windows per LTS channel), respect rollout gates (SLO degradation, error-rate, observability health), and provide deterministic simulation output for runbook signoff.

Design overview:
- Allocation slab: before starting drains, allocate a conservative capacity slab (expressed as GPU-slot-seconds) from the pool. This slab is withheld from eviction and used to absorb production traffic during upgrade.
- Tenant-aware reservations: use recent 5m consumption profiles to compute per-tenant soft reservations (pct of slab) for highest-QoS tenants. Reservations are best-effort and decay if underutilized.
- Autoscaler handshake: the allocator negotiates a temporary scale-up budget with the autoscaler controller via a new API (ScaleBudget request). The controller may grant immediate ephemeral nodes or prefer capacity-preserving drain pacing.
- Drain pace controller: progressive, not all nodes at once. Drain pacing uses target "drain rate" computed from slab size, current inflight load, and allowed latency delta.
- Rollout gates: pre-upgrade checks include per-route p50/p95 tokens, error-rate thresholds, service-health score from console. During rollout we evaluate sliding-window SLOs; if any gate trips, pause and automatically roll back drains for the last N nodes.
- LTS channels: channel config affects the aggressiveness of allocation (e.g., LTS-stable = higher preserved slab, smaller drain concurrency).
- Simulation harness: a deterministic simulator using historic request traces to predict delta in latency and required slab. The simulator runs as part of PR checks for allocator changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- No sustained loss of capacity (>2m) seen in canary upgrades across 10 synthetic tenant mixes.
- Latency regressions limited to configurable delta (default +15% p95) during upgrades, otherwise automatic pause.
- Autoscaler grant/deny path exercised in test harness; allocator handles denial by reducing concurrency.
- New metrics emitted: upgrade.allocator.{state,slab_size,drain_rate,pause_reasons,autoscaler_grants} and surfaced in console.
- Runbook and rollback SOP documented (link in links).

Implementation tasks (high level):
1) New allocator service and API spec (ScaleBudget/ReleaseBudget/DrainProgress).
2) Autoscaler changes to accept ScaleBudget requests and respond with grant levels or denial reasons.
3) Drain pace controller integrated into node-drain flow; node-drain honors a controller token before eviction.
4) Tenant reservation calculator with decay policy and config knobs.
5) Rollout gate evaluator, pluggable for future health signals.
6) Simulation harness and unit/integration tests including synthetic workloads and recorded traces.
7) Observability: metrics, console panels, alert rules.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Conservatism vs. upgrade speed: higher preserved slabs mean slower upgrades. We'll default to conservative for stable LTS and faster for edge channels.
- Complexity: introduces cross-controller coordination; require strong testing and canarying.
- Cost: temporary autoscaler grants increase cost; budget limits and pre-approval gates will be required for scheduled upgrades.

Open questions:
- How to surface tenant opt-out for low-priority workloads? Proposed: tenant label "upgrade-defer" that deprioritizes reservations.
- Exact autoscaler API shape and auth boundaries for private deployments.

Deliverables: allocator service prototype, updated autoscaler, drain-flow integration, simulator results, PRs, runbook, console dashboards, and a staged rollout plan for runtime-1.20 LTS.

2026-03-06: Architecture review: security requested clarification on auth for ScaleBudget API for Private customers. Action: include KMS-signed tokens for cross-service auth (owner: security).

2026-03-08: Implemented drain pace controller prototype (branch: allocator/prototype). Observed reduced p95 spike in synthetic test by 40% vs naive drain; still seeing short p50 jitter that scheduler team will investigate.
2026-03-09: Design review with PM (Leah Park) - agreed LTS conservative defaults and an "expedite" flag for emergency maintenance with manual approval flow.
2026-03-10: Integrating autoscaler handshake mock into CI; flakey test observed when autoscaler denies budget - allocator now reduces concurrency and retries with backoff (PR updated).
2026-03-11: QA requested: add deterministic seed to simulator and include a recorded 'hot-tenant' trace to validate worst-case. Added to test matrix.
2026-03-12: UX asked for two console widgets: live upgrade progress and predicted impact chart. Created ticket DES-2143 for the front-end work and linked below.
2026-03-14: Action items for next cycle: finalize ScaleBudget API, complete autoscaler change, add e2e test with k8s-integration, run blue-green canary on one dedicated pool.
